newsitem.title: USA: NYS revs from personal income taxes flat thru July.
newsitem.headline: NYS revs from personal income taxes flat thru July.

text.p: New York State's collections from personal income taxes were flat in the first four months of the 1998 fiscal year, when the effect of last year's huge surplus is excluded, the state comptroller said Friday.

The state ended the 1997 fiscal year on March 31 with a whopping $1.9 billion surplus. However, when strict, Generally Approved Accounting Practices are applied, the state faces a projected $979 million operating deficit, according to a report by the New York State Division of Budget.

New York State spent $19.2 billion in the first four months, but the state had no budget during this period, as lawmakers failed to approve a new one for fiscal 1998 until early August, over four months late.
"We can't wait any longer to reform our dysfunctional budget process to put an end to these growing budget delays," said the state comptroller, in prepared remarks.
McCall added that spending comparisons with the state's financial plan were not meaningful because it was prepared with preliminary results.

During the first four months of fiscal 1998, tax reductions pushed personal income tax witholding down four percent when measured against the year-ago period. Estimated personal income tax payments, however, leaped 14.9 percent.
For all governmental funds, sales tax collections were up 6.2 percent against the year-ago period, while total consumer taxes and fees rose 5.2 percent to $3.2 billion.

Business taxes were down 5.9 percent to $1.7 billion. Other taxes were up 33.3 percent to $560.4 million, mainly due to rises in estate and gift taxes. McCall noted estate and gift taxes often fluctuate after high-value estates are settled.
Miscellaneous recipts decreased slightly to $2.4 billion and federal funds rose 4.5 percent to $6.8 billion.
Disbursements from all governmental funds climbed 3.6 percent to $19.2 billion compared to a year-ago.

Departmental operations increased 10.5 percent to $3.9 billion, local aid stayed at last year's $12.7 billion level, general state charges rose 3.2 percent to $866 million, debt service increased 28.1 percent to $835 million, and spending for capital projects was up 12.7 percent to $942 million.
